questions: What two numbers do you multiply to get the work done on the crate?
Why is no work done when the crate does not move, even though the force is real?
segments.say: Work: force times distance. Watch the crate: a 50-newton force pushes it 4 metres along the floor, so the work done is 50 times 4 = 200 joules. Now imagine the crate wedged so it will not budge: push as hard as you like, the distance is zero and the work is zero. Keep your student notes open at the work and joule definitions for this scene.

questions: What changed between the two runs - the work, or the time?
If the same work took 4 seconds instead, what would the power be?
segments.say: Power: how fast is the work done? It is the same 200 joules both times. Slowly, over 10 seconds, the power is 200 over 10 = 20 watts. Fast, over 2 seconds, it is 200 over 2 = 100 watts. The work never changed - only the clock did. Now try the power question on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: Where is the energy before the mass is released, and where is it just before landing?
What would the KE be halfway down, when half the GPE has gone?
segments.say: Energy is conserved: GPE becomes KE. The 2-kilogram mass sits 5 metres up holding 98 joules of gravitational potential energy. Let it fall: watch the GPE drain away as the KE grows by the same amount, until at the bottom all 98 joules are kinetic. The total stayed 98 joules the whole way down - nothing was lost. Check the GPE and KE definitions in your student notes.

questions: Name two forms the petrol's chemical energy becomes as the car moves.
Why does the car stopping not prove that energy was destroyed?
segments.say: Check the thinking. The car stops when the petrol runs out, and it feels as if the energy has been destroyed. Follow it instead: the chemical energy became kinetic energy plus heat, some escaping as heat - every joule is still somewhere, just in a new form. Then take the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits the used-up claim head-on.
segments.watchFor: Energy gets used up when work is done. Listen for it in pair talk and watch for it on the exit ticket: The car runs out of petrol and stops, so the energy feels destroyed. Send them back to the falling mass and the correct turn: Energy is never used up: it changes form, like chemical energy becoming kinetic energy plus heat.
